Regret the tone of my post on data centers yesterday.

What I should have said:

There were reasonable concerns about data centers 18ish months ago: water, taxes, jobs, electricity prices, the environment and what they would do to small towns.

Well-structured data center projects have largely addressed these concerns today and we should be celebrating this.

On balance, data centers are awesome for America in every way.

On water: U.S. data centers use a fraction of what golf courses use. A lot of the numbers from 18 months ago were off by over 1000x. Newer data centers use closed-loop systems or recycled water. Should be required by every town approving a data center project.

On taxes: looking only at sales-tax exemptions, as Ronan Farrow did, is the wrong way to evaluate this. Data centers pay significant property taxes. Loudoun County, which is the wealthiest county in America, now collects on the order of $1 billion a year from data centers. In Quincy, WA, data centers are more than half the property-tax roll. Over time, property taxes can go to zero while government spending increases in these towns.

On jobs: this has been unambiguously awesome for blue collar Americans. Demand for electricians, plumbers, welders, HVAC techs, and contractors has gone vertical, and it is not a one-time construction job. These buildings get upgraded and expanded over time. That is why the building trades are fighting for them, and why some unions are now treating opposition to data centers as a reason not to endorse politicians.

On power: the original fear was that households would pay for the incremental electricity demand in the form of higher prices. That is why the ratepayer-protection deals and the new large-load tariffs exist. The right structure is: the data center brings or pays for new generation and signs a contract long enough that existing customers are protected. Where that is happening, utilities are cutting or freezing residential rates and saying so on the record.

Where it is not, people are right to object. Electricity prices are going down *today* in a number of large states because of data centers.

On the environment: data centers overwhelming use natural gas today, which is the cleanest power source outside of nuclear, solar and wind. And the companies that are building the data centers are committed to carbon neutrality such that an equivalent amount of solar will likely be built.

Maybe more importantly, the data centers need batteries to function effectively and these batteries can also sell energy back into the grid (which recently prevented blackouts in Texas).

Over time, data centers will run on solar plus batteries.

On the towns: Poverty in Quincy, WA fell from 29% to 6%. Data center taxes paid for a new high school, a hospital, a library, police and fire stations. This is happening in many left for dead former mill and farm towns that had no other bidder for the land.

Data centers are actually reindustrializing parts of America and creating the kind of working-class jobs both parties have spent decades claiming to support. That should not be a partisan issue. Data centers can and should be awesome for America and they increasingly, overwhelmingly are. Supporting the outsourcing of data centers to China will likely age just as well as support for the outsourcing of high quality, blue collar manufacturing jobs to China has aged.

When the facts change, I change my mind. I hope that reasonable people who had good faith reasons to oppose data centers at least consider updating their beliefs given the change in the facts over the last 18 months. This really matters for America.

I will say I also think the idea of making data centers beautiful is a good one that has yet to be implemented. Data centers should be just as beautiful as Grand Central Station. We can learn a lot from the railroad buildout. Neoclassical revival ftw.

Might write up open-weight AI tomorrow as this is equally essential to America.

Top tech investor Gavin Baker has publicly expressed regret over his earlier remakes dismissing opposition to data centers. In a post last week, Baker had written that ‘any politician opposed to data centers is unqualified to hold public office’, calling them a godsend for blue-collar workers and small towns. However, now Baker struck a a different tone, saying he regretted the phrasing and acknowledged that there were “reasonable concerns” about data centers around 18 months ago.Baker's earlier post declared that "nature is healing" on the data center debate, going as far as saying any politician opposed to data centers was unqualified to hold public office. In that post, he argued data centers were revitalizing small towns across America, delivering major benefits to blue-collar workers, lowering electricity costs, accelerating the shift to sustainable energy, and using only negligible amounts of water.In a follow-up post, Baker said he regretted the tone of his prior comments, offering a more measured version of his argument instead. He acknowledged that concerns about data centers were reasonable roughly 18 months ago, spanning issues like water usage, taxes, job creation, electricity prices, environmental impact, and effects on small towns. His revised position is that well-structured data center projects have since largely addressed those concerns, and that the industry's overall record now deserves to be seen as a positive for the country.Baker outlined how well-structured projects have since addressed worries over water usage, taxes, jobs, electricity prices, and environmental impact:•Water: U.S. data centers use far less water than golf courses, with newer facilities adopting closed-loop or recycled systems.•Taxes: While sales-tax exemptions drew criticism, Baker noted that property taxes from data centers have become a major revenue source in counties like Loudoun, VA and Quincy, WA.•Jobs: Demand for electricians, plumbers, welders, and HVAC technicians has surged, with unions now backing data center projects.•Power: Ratepayer-protection deals and large-load tariffs ensure households aren’t burdened by higher electricity costs. In some states, utilities have cut or frozen residential rates due to data center investments.•Environment: Facilities increasingly rely on natural gas, solar, and batteries, with commitments to carbon neutrality. Batteries also support grid stability, as seen in Texas.Impact on small townsBaker highlighted the transformation of towns like Quincy, WA, where poverty fell from 29% to 6% and tax revenues funded schools, hospitals, and libraries. He argued that data centers are “reindustrializing parts of America” and creating durable working-class jobs.Concluding his post, Baker said: “When the facts change, I change my mind. I hope that reasonable people who had good faith reasons to oppose data centers at least consider updating their beliefs given the change in the facts over the last 18 months.” He added that future projects should also focus on aesthetics, suggesting data centers be designed as beautifully as Grand Central Station.
Article Summary: Gavin Baker: Data centers are awesome for America in every way. Data centers use a fraction of what golf courses use, he says. Baker says he regrets the tone of his post on data centers yesterday. He says there were reasonable concerns about data centers 18ish months ago.

Article Title: OpenAI is touting ads as 'diversified business model' as it gears up for its massive IPO
Article Text:
OpenAI CEO Sam ​Altman

How OpenAI’s ad business started

Where Ads Are Rolling Out Now

OpenAI's guardrails on the Ads

What comes next

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI announced recently that its advertising business has reached a $1 billion annualised revenue rate, just 200 days after its launch, according to a report by CNBC. The company is positioning this milestone as a proof of its ‘diversified business model’ as it prepares for a massive initial public offering (IPO). OpenAI is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors, with ads now joining enterprise offerings, consumer subscriptions, and usage-based APIs as key revenue streams.OpenAI started testing ads inside ChatGPT in the US back in February this year, a move that was both widely anticipated and genuinely controversial. Digital advertising has long served as the primary profit engine for other tech giants like Google and Meta, but OpenAI's entry into that space drew direct mockery from its chief rival, Anthropic, which built its first-ever Super Bowl ad campaign specifically around contrasting itself with OpenAI's ad push.ChatGPT Ads are now live in more than 40 countries, and OpenAI said Monday it's expanding self-service access to advertisers across India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa.Recently, the company also announced the launch ChatGPT Ads in India. The company has revealed that it is expanding its advertising program to one of ChatGPT’s largest and most active markets. The company confirmed that the ads will roll out to logged‑in adults using the Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education subscriptions will remain ad‑free. WPP and Omnicom will be OpenAI’s first agency partners for ChatGPT Ads in India. With more than 50 brands set to go live this week, these agencies bring strong relationships across industries and expertise in strategy, creative, measurement, brand safety, and campaign execution. OpenAI said the model is non‑exclusive and it will continue to identify and work with other agencies.Within the chatbot, ads appear for users on OpenAI's Go subscription tier as well as its free tier — the free tier alone makes up the vast majority of ChatGPT's roughly 1 billion weekly active users, giving the ad business a massive built-in audience.OpenAI said its ads are clearly labeled and do not influence ChatGPT's actual answers to users. The company also said advertisers do not get access to users' private conversations, an apparent effort to get ahead of privacy concerns that have followed the rollout since its announcement in February.In a release, OpenAI said its next phase of growth will expand ChatGPT Ads into additional markets while introducing new ad formats, campaign objectives, buying options, and measurement tools for advertisers. The company also said it plans to explore new, more native ways for businesses to interact directly with consumers inside ChatGPT.
Article Summary: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI announced recently that its advertising business has reached a $1 billion annualised revenue rate. The company is positioning this milestone as a proof of its ‘diversified business model’ as it prepares for a massive initial public offering (IPO)

Article Title: Elon Musk's $60 billion purchase of Cursor that has made Sam Altman 'upset' has an 'indian connection', Aman Sanger
Article Text:
Who is Aman Sanger

Who is Aman Sanger

SpaceX acquire Cursor

OpenAI ends relationship with Cursor

Elon Musk’s $60 billion acquisition of Cursor has put the AI coding startup and its co-founder Aman Sanger in the spotlight, with the deal also drawing attention in India because of Sanger’s family roots. Aman Sanger, who was born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, co-founded Cursor in 2022 after studying computer science at MIT. The AI coding company grew rapidly before being acquired by Musk’s SpaceX, with its founders reportedly receiving billions of dollars in SpaceX shares. The deal has also added another layer to Musk’s rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman who recently called off its partnership with Cursor.For the 26-year-old Sanger, however, the story goes beyond the Musk-Altman feud, with his Indian family background adding an unexpected connection to the blockbuster AI deal.Born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, Aman Sanger grew up in a household where academic achievement and business success were strongly encouraged. His father, Arvind Sanger, graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay with a B. Tech degree in 1984 before moving to US. He later earned an MBA from Tulane University and built a successful career on Wall Street. His mother, Shilpa became an angel investor through the investment network Golden Seeds.She also took on a business management role at Geosphere Capital.Aman Sanger started coding at the age of 14 and developed an early interest in technology. After enrolling at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), he studied computer science between 2018 and 2022.Sanger cofounded Cursor, the maker of a popular AI code editing tool, with three friends from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2022. Before starting his own company, Sanger gained experience through internships at Google and Bridgewater Associates. He also launched an AI consultancy before joining fellow MIT students Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark to create Cursor in 2022.According to Forbes latest estimate, Aman Sanger has a net worth of over $2.5 billion.Last month, the company was acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion. Forbes estimates that each Cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion at the deal's closing.Before the SpaceX acquisition, Cursor claimed to have more than $1 billion in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest growing AI startups. Today, millions of software developers at enterprises like Nvidia, Adobe, Uber, Shopify and PayPal use Cursor to generate and edit chunks of code.Last week, OpenAI pulled its models out of Cursor, with a proposed shutoff date of November 12, 2026. There is no dispute here about pricing, performance or usage limits. The stated reason was the SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and OpenAI put that in writing in a public blog post rather than letting it leak out through a support page.OpenAI claims that X, formerly Twitter and now folded into SpaceX, broke the terms of its contract after Musk took over the platform. It also points to sworn testimony this year in which Musk acknowledged that xAI, likewise now part of SpaceX, had violated OpenAI's terms of service. OpenAI added that its forthcoming model, Astra, raises the accountability bar further, which is why it would rather end the arrangement than extend it to a partner it does not trust. It says it gave the maximum notice its contract allows so developers get time to plan.
Article Summary: Aman Sanger, 26, was born in the US to Indian immigrant parents. He co-founded Cursor, the maker of a popular AI code editing tool, with three friends from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2022. Forbes estimates that each Cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says farmers, doctors, teachers shouldn’t be profit-driven: ‘No one ever becomes a …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu says farmers do not choose farming for money

Sridhar Vembu says economics may view this behaviour differently

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has once again questioned the idea that every profession should be driven by profit, arguing that some of the most important jobs in society are built on duty, service and personal commitment. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Sridhar Vembu pointed to farmers, doctors, teachers and priests as examples of professions where money is often not the main reason people choose the work. His comments came a day after he questioned whether society really wants these professions to become profit-driven. Vembu argued that these professions form an important foundation of civilization and that businesses have a role in supporting them rather than treating profit as the only measure of value.Sridhar Vembu began his latest post by asking readers to consider why people choose certain professions. “Ask a farmer who made a choice to be in farming and they would tell you it is their love of farming,” he wrote.He argued that farmers are unlikely to describe money as the main reason they entered agriculture. Instead, he said, farmers may leave the profession when they can no longer afford to continue.Vembu also used doctors as an example. He said doctors are expected to follow professional and ethical rules that put patients first.According to Vembu, doctors who enter the profession mainly for money are not respected by their peers.He made a similar argument about teachers. “No one ever becomes a teacher because the money is good,” Vembu wrote. Vembu also included priests in the same group, arguing that people do not generally train for such roles because they expect financial rewards.Sridhar Vembu then turned his criticism toward economic models. “Economic models would consider all of that behaviour irrational,” he wrote. However, he argued that this willingness to pursue work for reasons beyond money is essential to society. “Yet without that deeply evolved character trait in humanity, civilization itself would collapse.”The Zoho founder's comments build on a broader argument he made in his previous X post about profit, capitalism and society. A day earlier, Vembu had asked: “Do we want our farmers, teachers, doctors and priests to be profit-driven?” He argued that modern finance and economic theory often pushes people toward making more activities profit-driven.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu questions idea that every profession should be driven by profit. He argues that some of the most important jobs in society are built on duty, service and personal commitment. He used farmers, doctors, teachers and priests as examples of professions where money is not the main reason people choose the work.

Article Title: In 1998, Steve Jobs convinced a 37-year-old Tim Cook to join near-bankrupt Apple, here's the 'story' he told to make him leave world's biggest PC company
Article Text:
When Steve Jobs convinced a 37-year-old Tim Cook to join near-bankrupt Appl

Steve Jobs’ vision of the iMac G3

Tim Cook ignored ‘career advice’ from peers

Apple hired Tim Cook in March 1998

Tim Cook concluded his 15-year tenure as Apple ’s CEO on August 31, 2026, transitioning to executive chairman of the board effective September 1, 2026. John Ternus, formerly senior vice president of hardware engineering, has officially taken the helm of the company. While Cook leaves behind an era defined by monumental commercial success, his beginnings at the company were far more modest. Back in early 1998, Apple was on the edge of financial collapse, struggling with plunging staff morale, and widely viewed as an undesirable employer across Silicon Valley. Yet, Steve Jobs managed to convince a 37-year-old rising executive to walk away from Compaq, which was then the global leader in personal computer sales, and join the struggling company.Before making the leap, Cook had built an extensive corporate resume, spending 12 years at IBM alongside key executive roles at Intelligent Electronics and Compaq. While Cook had repeatedly rejected outreach from Apple's recruitment team, he eventually agreed to a face-to-face sit-down with Jobs. Cook later explained to Charlie Rose in 2014 that he felt compelled to meet the person who had essentially built the modern computing industry and was pursuing a distinctive vision.During their introductory discussion, Jobs reportedly laid out his roadmap to revitalise Apple, describing an upcoming computer concept designed to upend the entire PC landscape. CNBC reported that Jobs shared preliminary details of a hardware design unlike anything on the market. The concept later materialised as the iMac G3, the vibrant, translucent computer that turned designer Jony Ive into an industry star.Cook walked away from the encounter fascinated by the design and convinced that collaborating alongside Jobs would represent the privilege of a lifetime.Taking the role required Cook to defy the advice of his closest peers and all conventional logic. Reflecting on the decision during his 2010 Auburn University commencement address, Cook noted that any logical cost-benefit evaluation favoured staying at Compaq. One chief executive even warned Cook that leaving the market leader for Apple would be foolish.Cook believed that following the crowd was a mistake. Recognizing the deep operational challenges facing Apple, he decided he could make a meaningful impact and trusted his intuition over traditional career calculations.In March 1998, Jobs formally appointed Cook as senior vice president of worldwide operations, providing him a base compensation of $400,000 alongside a $500,000 signing bonus. Cook took charge of completely overhauling Apple’s supply chain, manufacturing systems and global distribution.Cook’s procurement and operations background proved to be an ideal match for Apple's recovery and for Jobs' management approach. Speaking to biographer Walter Isaacson for the book Steve Jobs, the late Apple co-founder reflected on their dynamic:“He had the same vision I did. We could interact at a high strategic level, and I could just forget about a lot of things unless he came and pinged me.”
Article Summary: Tim Cook concluded his 15-year tenure as Apple’s CEO on August 31, 2026. John Ternus, formerly senior vice president of hardware engineering, has officially taken the helm of the company. Back in early 1998, Apple was on the edge of financial collapse, struggling with plunging staff morale. Yet, Steve Jobs managed to convince a 37-year-old rising executive to walk away from Compaq, which was then the global leader in personal computer sales.

Article Title: Government sounds alarm, ads on Facebook ‌and Instagram found directing users to apps that steal banking passwords and remotely control users' phones
Article Text:
How these apps work, spy and steal

How to uninstall these apps

The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. In an advisory, National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said that it has observed a rise in financial frauds perpetrated through malicious Android apps masquerading as pornography apps, circulated through Facebook and Instagram ads. As per the Ministry of Home Affairs advisory, these Android apps are operating under the names "Night Play", "Reloop", "Kyss", “Vimo”, “Rivo”, “Nexo”, “Vixa” and other similar variants.These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content, where the user is prompted to download an APK file. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device. Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to malicious/criminal activity. As per government warning, these apps can secretly access information stored on users' phones, capture one-time passwords and bank PINs, and transfer money from ​accounts without the owner's knowledge. Not just this, the apps also make it difficult for users to uninstall them through device's normal settings.Distribution: The malicious apps are distributed through pornographic content related advertisements or links majorly on Facebook and Instagram. These ads redirect to phishing websites.Redirection: Ads redirect to phishing websites serving pornographic content. Domains of the website majorly belong to “.live”. Users are persuaded to download and install the APK from sources outside the Google Play Store.App Update: A secondary package gets downloaded and installed on the pretext of an app update, based on permissions abused by the first, initial app.Abuse of Accessibility Permission for device takeover: After installation, the app asks users to grant Accessibility and other sensitive permissions. Once enabled, the malware gains control of the device and continues to run in the background.VPN Installation: Some apps may also install a VPN on the device, thereby routing all internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. This compromises user's transmitted data, which may subsequently be exploited for malicious or criminal activities.Unauthorized Transactions: Since the malware has the ability to take over the compromised device, installing such apps may lead to financial fraud.METHOD 1: Safe Mode RebootStep 1: Start Your Phone in Safe Mode: Press and hold the Power button. Press and hold Power Off until the Safe Mode option appears. Click OK or Restart in Safe Mode. Wait for the phone to restart. "Safe Mode" will appear at the bottom of the screen.Step 2: Uninstall the App: Open Settings. Go to Apps. Select the suspicious application. Tap Uninstall. Remove any other unknown or related apps.Step 3: Restart Normally: Restart the phone. The device will exit Safe Mode automatically.Second MethodStep 1: Restore the Default Home Screen (If required): Open Settings. Go to Apps → Default Apps → Home App. Select your phone's original launcher (System Launcher, One UI Home, Pixel Launcher, etc.).Step 2: Disable Accessibility Access: Open Settings. Tap Accessibility. Open Installed Services or Downloaded Apps. Select the suspicious application. Turn Accessibility Off.Step 3: Remove Administrator Access: Open Settings. Go to Security or Security & Privacy.Open Device Admin Apps or Device Administrators. If the suspicious app is enabled, select it. Tap Deactivate or Turn Off.Verify the Device: Open Settings > Apps. Confirm that the suspicious application has been removed. If the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data and perform a Factory Reset.
Article Summary: The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device.

Article Title: Canada has important information for international students: Starting September 1, we are changing the …
Article Text:
Canada student visa: Who's affected and by how much

The new dollar amounts

Family Members Amount Required (Sept 1 onward) Increase 1 (principal applicant) CAD $23,448 +$553 2 CAD $29,192 +$690 3 CAD $35,888 +$848 4 CAD $43,572 +$1,029 5 CAD $49,419 +$1,167 6 CAD $55,736 +$1,316 7 CAD $62,054 +$1,465 Each additional member CAD $6,318 +$148

What counts as acceptable proof of funds

Separate, higher requirements for Quebec

Canada has introduced higher financial requirements for international students applying for study permits starting today (September 1). According to the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, applicants must now show increased proof of funds to demonstrate their ability to support themselves during their studies. The change is aimed at reflecting rising living costs and ensuring that students are financially prepared. This new requirement put forward by IRCC sets the cost-of-living proof at 75% of Statistics Canada’s Low Income Cut-Off (LICO), in addition to tuition and travel expenses. "Important information for international students: starting September 1, 2026, the amount of funds you will need to demonstrate when applying for a study permit will increase. We update the financial resource requirements applicable to study permit applicants each year to adjust them to the cost of living and to help protect international students from any exploitation," wrote IRCC in a post shared on X (formerly knonw as Twitter).For a single applicant outside Quebec, the minimum proof of funds has risen to CAD $23,448, an increase of $553 over the previous threshold. The amounts scale higher depending on family size, with applicants required to show additional funds for each dependent.In Quebec, students must meet separate financial thresholds tied to the Quebec Acceptance Certificate (QAC). As of January 1, 2026, a single applicant must show CAD $24,617, with higher requirements for families.The increase applies to applicants intending to study anywhere in Canada outside Quebec, which has its own separate requirements. A single applicant with no dependants will need to show $553 more than under the previous threshold. Larger families face steeper jumps — an applicant bringing six additional family members will need $1,465 more than before.These cost-of-living figures are added on top of whatever amount is already required to cover the first full year of tuition and travel to and from Canada, meaning the total financial bar for approval is rising across the board, not just the cost-of-living component in isolation.According to the immigration department's updated guidance, published August 28, 2026, the new required amounts by family size are as follows:•1 applicant (principal only): $23,448 (up $553)•2 family members: $29,192 (up $690)•3 family members: $35,888 (up $848)•4 family members: $43,572 (up $1,029)•5 family members: $49,419 (up $1,167)•6 family members: $55,736 (up $1,316)•7 family members: $62,054 (up $1,465)•Each additional family member beyond seven: $6,318 (up $148)Applications submitted before September 1, 2026 will still be assessed under the previous cost-of-living amounts that were in effect at the time they were received. Applicants whose study programs run longer than one year must also explain how they intend to fund the remainder of their studies beyond that first year.IRCC accepts documentation across three broad categories. The first covers fees already paid, such as a receipt showing tuition and housing costs have been settled — though this must still be paired with separate evidence of funds available for living and travel expenses.The second category covers funds currently available, which can include proof of a student or education loan from a bank, a Canadian bank account in the student's name showing transferred funds, a guaranteed investment certificate from a Canadian bank, bank statements from the past six months (Canadian or foreign), pension plan documentation, or proof of rental income.The third category covers expected or promised support, including proof of a scholarship or a Government of Canada-funded education program, recent pay stubs, or a letter from a financial supporter. That letter must confirm the supporter's relationship to the applicant, their occupation, any dependants they have, and the specific amount of support they intend to provide — along with supporting evidence verifying the applicant's connection to that person and a copy of the supporter's identification or business registration.IRCC notes these examples aren't exhaustive, and applicants may need to provide additional documentation depending on their country and individual circumstances. Applicants from countries with foreign exchange controls must also show they'll be permitted to export the necessary funds to Canada.Students planning to study in Quebec face a different process entirely. They must first obtain a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (QAC) before applying to IRCC for a study permit, and must meet Quebec-specific living expense requirements that are notably higher than the federal amounts. Those figures, last updated January 1, 2026, range from $24,617 for a single applicant up to $60,299 for six family members, with each additional family member requiring $5,254 — figures that, notably, don't include tuition or transportation costs.Both the Quebec provincial government and the federal government assess an applicant's proof of financial support, but they evaluate the same pool of funds — applicants aren't required to show separate or additional funds for the federal IRCC assessment on top of what they've already demonstrated to Quebec.
Article Summary: Canada has introduced higher financial requirements for international students applying for study permits starting today. The change is aimed at reflecting rising living costs and ensuring that students are financially prepared. For a single applicant outside Quebec, the minimum proof of funds has risen to CAD $23,448.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg buys 440-acre castle estate in Ireland; spokesperson says: Mark and his family are excited to continue caring for ...
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg now has a 440-acre home in Ireland

Mark Zuckerberg's Ireland connection goes beyond the castle

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have bought a castle estate in Ireland that covers around 440 acres. The couple will use Strancally Castle in County Waterford as a home during their visits to the country, where Meta has its international headquarters. While the price of the private deal has not been disclosed, the Irish Times estimated the property's value at between €20 million and €30 million. Confirming the purchase, a spokesperson said: “Mark and his family are excited to continue caring for this historic home and look forward to spending time in Ireland, where Meta maintains its international headquarters.”Strancally Castle sits on a 178-hectare, or roughly 440-acre, estate in County Waterford. Mark Zuckerberg and wife Priscilla Chan bought the property to use as a base when they visit Ireland. The purchase adds Ireland to the list of places connected to Zuckerberg, whose company has had a major presence in the country for years.Strancally Castle was built in 1830 for John Keily, a former Conservative Member of Parliament. It was designed by architects James and George Richard Pain. The large scale of the property is reflected in one detail mentioned in the book The Houses of Ireland: walking from the dining room to the kitchen could take four and a half minutes.It is located in the Blackwater Valley, an area known for its historic estates and large country homes.Before the sale to Zuckerberg and Chan, the estate was owned by Michael Alen-Buckley, co-founder of London-based investment firm RAB Capital, and his wife Giancarla. The couple bought the property in the early 2000s and carried out restoration work.In a statement, they said they were grateful for the opportunity to save and restore Strancally Castle during the 25 years they owned it. They also said they were pleased that Zuckerberg and his family intended to continue maintaining the property and its grounds.For Mark Zuckerberg, the purchase is also linked to Meta's long-standing presence in Ireland. The company maintains its international headquarters in the country, making visits to Ireland part of its global operations.Strancally Castle will now serve as a family base during those visits. Nearly two centuries after it was built, the 440-acre estate has found its latest owner in one of the world's best-known technology executives, with Zuckerberg's spokesperson saying the family plans to continue caring for the historic home.
Article Summary: Strancally Castle was built in 1830 for John Keily, a former Conservative Member of Parliament. The price of the private deal has not been disclosed, but the property's value is estimated at between €20 million and €30 million. The purchase adds Ireland to the list of places connected to Zuckerberg, whose company has had a major presence in the country.

Article Title: As Google renames 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US; company's 'update' on what users in the US, Canada and 'rest of the world' will see
Article Text:
Google statement on the name chang

Canada PM Mark Carney on US renaming the Lake Ontario

Trump sends direct message to Apple to change the name

Escalating the trade dispute with Canada, US President Donald Trump last week announced that he was changing the name of the smallest of the five Great Lakes. As the trade talks between the US and Canada broke down, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'.After Trump's announcement, Google began rolling out this change for US users. The company posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses."The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S.,people using Maps in the U.S. will see "Lake America," those in Canada will continue to see "Lake Ontario," and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names. These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now," said the company in a blog update.In a post on X, formerly Twitter, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney wrote, "The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big”. The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms. Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario – then, now and always."President Trump has reportedly "reached out to Apple directly" about changing Lake Ontario's name to Lake America in Apple Maps. According to US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, “The president reached out to Apple directly, so I’m sure that we may be seeing that change coming up soon to Lake America.” Burgum shared the same in an ‌interview ⁠on Fox Business’ “Mornings with Maria” programme.
Article Summary: The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America' Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see 'Lake Ontario'

Article Title: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook sends memo to employees; says: I am not leaving Apple, but I am...
Article Text:
Tim Cook signs off as Apple CEO after 15 years, hands over to John Ternus.

Tim Cook hands Apple to John Ternus, a hardware man and not a services one

Tim Cook is not leaving Apple, he is changing desks

Here's Tim Cook's final memo to Apple employees, in full

Team,

Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words.

I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn’t let this day pass without sending a note to you to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you’ve sent my way, for the way you’ve shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader.

The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that.

There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here.

It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day.

Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that’s the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our “dent in the universe,” as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world.

How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am.

As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership.

I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make.

I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world.

With all I have and all I am, I am always.

Yours,

Tim

Tim Cook signed off as Apple chief executive on Monday the way he ran the company for 15 years, calmly and with the credit pushed elsewhere. In a farewell memo to Apple employees on his final day in the job, Cook wrote that this was a moment he always knew would come, and that it was still hard to believe he was writing the words. John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO on September 1.The Tim Cook memo is notable for what it leaves out. There is no product tease, no roadmap, and no mention of AI, regulation or China, the three pressures that will shape Ternus's first year. Instead Cook spends most of it thanking staff, arguing that Apple's culture is the thing an annual report can never capture, and reaching back to Steve Jobs and his line about leaving a dent in the universe. The sentence employees were waiting for came late. He is not leaving Apple, he said, only stepping away from a role he has loved deeply.Cook saved his warmest paragraph for his successor. He called Ternus brilliant and capable, and said few people understand what it takes to build world-changing products the way Ternus does. Coming from a CEO long accused of running Apple like an operations manager, the choice of words is pointed.Ternus has been senior vice president of hardware engineering, overseeing the entire device line-up.Recent launches under him include the ultra-thin iPhone Air, the cheaper MacBook Neo, and AirPods with hearing health features. Apple also pulled its Mac mini and Mac Studio releases earlier in the year to meet AI-driven demand. The promotion reads as a bet on hardware execution rather than a pivot to services.From Tuesday, Cook becomes executive chairman of Apple's board. He keeps the portfolio he was best at, managing governments in Washington and Beijing, at a point when tariff demands and political requests are landing on Apple's desk with some regularity.Cook took over from Jobs in August 2011. The 15 years since brought the Apple Watch, AirPods, and a vastly expanded iPhone, iPad and Mac business. On X, he told the Apple community that his title changes on Tuesday but his affection for them will not, and signed the memo: "With all I have and all I am, I am always. Yours, Tim."
Article Summary: Tim Cook signs off as Apple CEO after 15 years, hands over to John Ternus. Tim Cook memo is notable for what it leaves out. There is no product tease, no roadmap, and no mention of AI, regulation or China. Cook spends most of it thanking staff, arguing that Apple's culture is the most important thing.

Article Title: Chinese chipmaker that sued Pentagon makes breakthrough in memory chips
Article Text:
CXMT is China's leading producer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips.

CXMT latest memory hardware attracts big Chinese players

Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has reportedly made a breakthrough in advanced memory chips even as the tech industry is witnessing unprecedented demand for RAMs. As per a report by The Information (via news agency Reuters), the company has started manufacturing advanced high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in limited volumes. Citing two people familiar with the development, the report revealed that CXMT is producing HBM3E, an advanced class of high-bandwidth memory silicon essential for powering artificial intelligence (AI) hardware.The semiconductor manufacturer aims to ramp up larger-scale mass production by 2027, the report added. Multiple domestic semiconductor design firms are already evaluating CXMT’s latest memory hardware to integrate with their proprietary computing silicon.Prominent Chinese tech players, including Alibaba Group’s chip-design division T-Head and Beijing-based Cambricon Technologies, are said to be actively testing the HBM3E components alongside their in-house AI processors.If ongoing qualification testing succeeds, these technology firms plan to integrate CXMT's memory modules into commercial products as early as next year, the report pointed out.Recently, China's largest memory chipmaker sued the Pentagon after the company was placed on a list of companies the US government says support China's military. The lawsuit marks the latest escalation between Beijing's tech sector and Washington over trade restrictions tied to national security concerns.“CXMT is not affiliated with the Chinese military. CXMT designs, produces, and sells its DRAM chips for civilian and commercial use, not for military use,” the company said in its federal lawsuit. The US Defense Department declined to comment on the specifics of the case, saying, “As a matter of policy, the Department does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation.”CXMT has also recently drawn attention after Apple reportedly made a special request to US officials regarding its status. The Cupertino-based tech giant has also reportedly held early talks with CXMT for iPhones and MacBooks which will be sold within the Chinese market.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has reportedly made a breakthrough in advanced memory chips. The company has started manufacturing advanced high- bandwidth memory (HBM) in limited volumes. Multiple domestic semiconductor design firms are already evaluating CXMT’s latest memory hardware to integrate with their proprietary computing silicon.

Article Title: In 2025, researchers used fired clay bricks and eggshell waste, reducing energy consumption for heating and cooling by 50%, turning food waste into useful building material
Article Text:
AI generated Image for representational purpose

How eggshell waste was added to clay bricks

10% eggshell bricks showed the biggest drop in heat transfer

The waste problem is part of the attraction

A pile of discarded eggshells could have a surprising second life: inside building bricks. In 2025, researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. As part of the study, researchers then found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. The study found that bricks containing 10% eggshell waste and fired at 1,100°C recorded a 50% reduction in thermal conductivity compared with ordinary clay bricks. Researchers also found that the thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity also fell by about 30%.The researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. The powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis. Researchers used different proportions of eggshells ranging from 1% to 10%.The study found that eggshells changed the internal structure of the bricks. During high-temperature firing, calcium carbonate in the eggshells breaks down and releases carbon dioxide. This process helps create pores inside the material.The strongest thermal result came from the brick containing 10% eggshell waste. Compared to the untreated clay brick, the researchers recorded a 50% drop in thermal conductivity, meaning less heat could pass through the material.Thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity each fell by about 30%, the research found.The results, researchers believe, can have significance for buildings in hot climates, where walls absorb and transfer heat from the outside into indoor spaces. Bricks with more air spaces can slow heat movement because air is a poor conductor of heat. The researchers found that adding eggshell waste changed the brick's internal structure and density, creating conditions that improved its insulation performance.The study also pointed to another potential benefit: recycling eggshells instead of sending them to landfills. The researchers noted that more than 110 billion eggshells are estimated to end up in landfills worldwide. Turning some of this waste into construction material could give it a useful purpose while reducing the need for some raw materials.
Article Summary: Researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. Found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. Researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis.

Article Title: California passes bill that won't require Linux and other open-source systems to follow the state's age verification law
Article Text:
Representative Image

How the amendment redefines who the law covers

"operating system provider"

"under license terms that permit a recipient to copy, redistribute, and modify the software."

"offered to consumers as a stand-alone executable application through a covered application store"

Fixing a definition that classified every adult as a child

"user,"

"a child that is the primary user of a device,"

What remains covered, and what's not still unclear

California's legislature has passed Assembly Bill 1856, exempting open-source operating systems from the state's Digital Age Assurance Act. The move comes months before the law is due to take effect on January 1, 2027. The California Senate amended and passed the bill this month in a 39-0 vote, and the Assembly accepted the changes in a concurrence vote soon after. The amendment ends almost a year of uncertainty surrounding whether Linux distributions and SteamOS would be forced to collect user age data during account setup alongside Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. AB 1856 has now been sent to Governor Gavin Newsom, who signed the original act into law last October.The amendments redefine the termto exclude any person or entity that distributes an OS or applicationAny software distributed under the GPL, MIT, BSD and Apache licenses satisfies that test, which removes the likes of Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu, Arch and the BSD family from AB 1856's scope.A second exclusion removes software components that aren'tfrom the law's definition of an application, covering libraries and dependencies distributed through package managers like apt and pacman.AB 1856 doesn't explicitly say that repos aren't app stores, but a store's main obligation under the law is to request an age signal from the user's OS provider and pass it to developers; an exempt open-source OS produces no signal.A third carve-out excludes storefronts distributing extensions or add-ons that run exclusively inside a host application, which takes browser extension stores out of scope.The amendments to AB 1856 also remove the original definition ofwhich read,and technically classified every device owner in California as a child.The law's signalling framework depends on adults declaring their age on account setup, so their devices get flagged as 18 and over, but under that definition nobody could ever be flagged as an adult. Left uncorrected, that wording would have undermined the entire mechanism the law relies on to distinguish adult users from minors.Lawmakers also inserted a new provision prohibiting anyone from requesting an age signal from an OS provider or app store unless required by law. That closes off potential abuse of the age API that could have led to it being used as a general-purpose data collection channel even when age verification wasn't required. Platforms and developers also gain a good-faith safe harbour against erroneous signals, protecting them from liability when age-gating signals are inaccurate.Windows, macOS, iOS and Android remain fully in scope, with age collection required at account setup from January 1, 2027. A later July 1, 2027 deadline applies to devices set up before January 1.Whether SteamOS is in scope isn't yet clear. Its Arch-based system components are open source, but Valve distributes the image alongside the proprietary Steam client, leaving its status under the amended law ambiguous.GrapheneOS, which in March said it would refuse to comply with age-verification mandates, is distributed under the open-source MIT and Apache licenses and now falls outside the law's scope entirely, though Brazil's Digital ECA still applies.Assembly member Buffy Wicks, who wrote both the Digital Age Assurance Act and the AB 1856 amendment, introduced the exemption back in February following criticism from Linux developers and the Electronic Frontier Foundation.
Article Summary: California legislature passes bill exempting open-source operating systems from Digital Age Assurance Act. The move comes months before the law is due to take effect on January 1, 2027. The amendment ends almost a year of uncertainty surrounding whether Linux distributions and SteamOS would be forced to collect user age data.

Article Title: In 2024, Netflix told shareholders it needed no partners; now its co-CEO Greg Peters says outside deals are ‘very promising’
Article Text:
Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters

"already operates as a go-to destination for entertainment.”

"very promising,"

"If we see additional deals that similarly serve our members, that work for our partner, that work for us, we'll certainly consider them,"

Netflix shifts its tone on partnerships

Other streaming giants are also racing to bundle

"The thing that matters is that when you turn on the TV, what app are you opening for the next three hours?"

Two years ago, Netflix told its shareholders that the companyThis made it clear that the streaming giant saw little need to feature rival services within its own app. Now, that position has softened considerably. Speaking on its latest earnings call, Netflix co-chief executive Greg Peters described the early results of a new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 asand signalled the company is open to striking similar deals elsewhere.Peters said.Netflix's moves have been more subtle than some of its rivals, but that could soon change. In June, the company began streaming TF1 in its French markets, including a live feed of TF1 networks and on-demand programs. It marked Netflix's first arrangement of its kind, and it appears to be a test case for something larger.A report by The New York Times cited three people familiar with the discussions, who said Netflix executives recently held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform.However, the people warned that no deal is imminent, and that it remains unclear whether Netflix would absorb the outside content directly into its own service, as in a recent YouTube-Peacock arrangement, or instead act more as a retailer, similar to how Amazon Prime Video operates.Netflix is not alone in this pivot. For years, Amazon has persuaded tens of millions of people to use its Prime Video app to subscribe to other services, like HBO Max or Apple TV, and to watch shows like "The Pitt" or "Ted Lasso" from within the retail giant's digital walls. Now, other streaming leaders are sprinting to catch up.YouTube and Roku are racing to become one-stop shops for all the content people watch on their televisions. People who pay for a commercial-free YouTube tier, for example, will soon have access to Peacock content like "The Traitors" and "Sunday Night Football" as part of a recent deal between the two companies.The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television. Companies that were once laser-focused on gaining new subscribers are now far more concerned with keeping those people watching as much as possible, and cancelling as little as possible. What were once described as the streaming wars have effectively morphed into bundling wars. The biggest streaming firms are no longer content to just have the most subscribers; they also want to be the main entry point to everything streaming has to offer.Jonathan Carson, chief executive of Antenna, a subscription research firm, told the NYT.Consumers already appear receptive to managing their subscriptions through a single platform. Over the last three years, subscriptions made via third-party platforms like Amazon, Roku or YouTube have grown roughly 60 per cent, according to Antenna, with about a third of all new subscriptions now purchased this way.
Article Summary: Netflix's new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 is "very promising," says co-CEO Greg Peters. The company has also held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform. The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television.

Article Title: Google, Microsoft and Apple's 'European troubles' now also become of OpenAI, Roblox and Reddit, as Europe cannot stop…
Article Text:
The EU has decided a chatbot that searches the web is a search engine

Compliance under the Digital Services Act means audits, risk reports and open data

The European Commission has added ChatGPT to the small club of online services it polices most closely, making OpenAI 's chatbot the first AI assistant to fall under the strictest tier of the Digital Services Act. In the same decision on Monday, Brussels designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms. The compliance headaches that Google , Microsoft and Apple have spent years managing in Europe now belong to three more American companies.ChatGPT has been classified as a Very Large Online Search Engine rather than a platform, and that is the part worth paying attention to. The Commission decided that a chatbot answering prompts by pulling live results off the web is doing a search engine's job, whatever the interface looks like. The three services have four months, until January 2027, to comply. The penalty ceiling for failing is six per cent of global annual turnover.The threshold for this tier is 45 million average monthly users in the EU, about one in ten people in the bloc. ChatGPT's search function reported roughly 159 million monthly users for the six months ending March 2026. Reddit declared 57.2 million and Roblox 46.6 million, which puts the gaming platform barely over the line.Companies self-declare these numbers, and all three did.EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the three services would now be held to a "higher standard of scrutiny and accountability", in line with their impact on citizens. The DSA's strictest tier now covers 28 platforms and search engines.The work ahead is unglamorous. Each service must run annual systemic risk assessments covering illegal content, harm to minors, users' physical and mental wellbeing, fundamental rights, elections and public security. They must also open themselves to independent audits and share data with regulators and vetted researchers. Ireland's Coimisiún na Meán will supervise ChatGPT and Reddit, while the Dutch consumer authority takes Roblox.OpenAI said it accepts that ChatGPT search operates as a search service under the DSA and is preparing for the extra requirements. Roblox called itself the first gaming platform to hit the milestone in the EU. Reddit did not comment.Brussels has already collected roughly 870 million euros in DSA fines, including 550 million from AliExpress in July and 120 million from X in December. Washington has called such penalties economic extortion and threatened retaliation. That argument is about to get louder, because the DSA has now reached generative AI, and the list of US companies with European troubles is three names longer.
Article Summary: ChatGPT is the first AI assistant to fall under the strictest tier of the Digital Services Act. The three services have four months, until January 2027, to comply. The penalty ceiling for failing is six per cent of global annual turnover.

Article Title: China and Netherlands continue to fight on chip giant Nexperia, now Chinese court freezes $300 million of company's assets
Article Text:
Chinese court freezes $300 million of Nexperia assets as Wingtech fight drags on

The lawsuit behind the asset freeze is asking for far more than $300 million

How a Dutch national security intervention became a Chinese courtroom fight

A Chinese court has frozen up to 2.14 billion yuan, roughly $300 million, in assets belonging to Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its equipment arm, handing the company's estranged Chinese owner fresh leverage in a dispute that has now run for close to a year. The order came from the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court and was disclosed by Wingtech Technology in a stock exchange filing, according to Reuters.The freeze covers Nexperia's stakes in four China-based businesses, including its semiconductor operations in China, Wuxi and Shanghai, plus the wholly owned Wuxi unit of its equipment arm. The measures took effect between August 20 and August 25 and stay in place until August 2029. The case has not gone to trial. On paper little has shifted: the board is unchanged and the ownership question is still open. What Wingtech has gained is pressure.Wingtech and a subsidiary filed suit in May, naming Nexperia, its equipment arm, the parent company and three executives. They are seeking 8 billion yuan in damages, arguing the defendants carried out or helped carry out discriminatory Dutch restrictions, and are leaning on China's Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law to make the case.Nexperia and its equipment arm did not immediately respond to requests for comment.This began last year when the Dutch government intervened at Nexperia over concerns that technology, funds and production assets could be moved abroad. The Enterprise Chamber suspended chief executive Zhang Xuezheng and placed the voting rights tied to Wingtech's shareholding under independent management. Beijing answered with export controls on Nexperia's China operations, which disrupted shipments of the cheap, unglamorous chips that cars and consumer electronics run on. Talks between Beijing and The Hague restored the flow of supply and the Netherlands suspended its order, but Wingtech never recovered its voting control.The split has already reshaped how the company makes chips. Nexperia's China unit, cut off from European wafers, said last week it is moving its entire product line to a domestic 12-inch wafer foundry supplied by an unnamed Chinese partner, shifting away from the 8-inch and 6-inch lines it ran before. Diodes, MOSFETs and logic ICs are all part of that move. China accounts for about 70 per cent of Nexperia's output.The freeze runs until August 2029 and the case has not been heard yet, so this could sit unresolved for years. By the time anyone wins the ownership argument, they may be inheriting two companies instead of one.
Article Summary: Wingtech Technology filed suit in May, naming Nexperia, its equipment arm, the parent company and three executives. They are seeking 8 billion yuan in damages, arguing the defendants carried out or helped carry out discriminatory Dutch restrictions. The freeze runs until August 2029 and the case has not been heard yet.
